title: Checkout API 5xx spike during promo traffic surge
symptoms: HTTP 503 rate rose from <0.1% to ~18% within 6 minutes; p99 latency > 12s; logs show 'timeout acquiring connection from pool' and 'remaining connection slots reserved'; DB CPU normal.
recent_changes: Marketing email campaign sent 15 minutes earlier; no deploys in prior 24h.
root_cause: [confirmed] Database connection pool exhausted: per-pod pool size x autoscaled pod count exceeded the database max_connections limit during the traffic surge.
resolution_steps: 1) Confirmed connection saturation via pool metrics and DB active-connection count | 2) Temporarily capped checkout-api max replicas to keep total connections under DB limit | 3) Reduced per-pod pool size from 40 to 20 | 4) Restarted the most starved pods after settings rolled out | 5) Watched 5xx rate and connection count for 30 minutes
outcome: 5xx returned to baseline in ~25 minutes. Follow-up: add a connection-budget check to capacity reviews and put a pooler in front of the DB.

title: Login failures in one region after signing key rotation

recent_changes: Scheduled JWT signing-key rotation ran at 03:15 UTC.

resolution_steps: 1) Compared key IDs served by each region's JWKS endpoint and found eu-west missing the new key ID | 2) Manually triggered JWKS cache refresh in eu-west | 3) Verified new tokens validated in eu-west | 4) Reviewed the failed refresh job logs and filed a bug for silent failure
outcome: Login success in eu-west normalized within 10 minutes of refresh. Alerting added for JWKS key-set mismatch across regions.

title: Search latency spike from long GC pauses

outcome: p99 latency returned to ~350ms. Follow-up: add heap-utilization alert and include index size in capacity planning.

title: User profile API slow after cache hit rate collapse
symptoms: p95 latency rose from 80ms to 1.4s; database read load doubled; Redis 'evicted_keys' counter climbing; cache hit rate fell from ~95% to ~40%.
recent_changes: A new feature added larger profile objects to the cache 3 days earlier.
root_cause: [confirmed] Redis reached maxmemory and began evicting hot keys because cached object size grew, reducing hit rate and pushing load to the DB.
resolution_steps: 1) Checked Redis memory and eviction metrics | 2) Scaled Redis to a larger memory tier | 3) Trimmed cached profile fields to those actually read by clients | 4) Monitored hit rate and DB read load until stable
outcome: Hit rate recovered to ~93%; latency back to baseline within an hour.

title: Order worker backlog from poison message crash loop

outcome: Backlog fully drained in ~40 minutes after workers recovered. Delayed orders were processed; no lost orders.

title: Notification emails delayed because consumers autoscaled to zero
